item.title: China holds exhibition to mark 90th anniversary of Long March victory
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
BEIJING, Sept. 22 (Xinhua) -- A themed exhibition commemorating the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March opened Tuesday at the Military Museum of the Chinese People's Revolution in Beijing. In his address at the opening ceremony, Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and a member of the Secretariat of the CPC Central Committee, said the victory stunned the world and continues to shine in the annals of history. Cai stressed that the victory of the Long March marked a great turning point for the CPC and the Chinese revolution, and stands as a towering monument in the historic process of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The Long March was an epic military trek from 1934 to 1936, during which the CPC-led Red Army broke through encirclement by Kuomintang forces. Red Army soldiers braved raging rivers, snow-covered mountains and treacherous grasslands, with some marching as far as 12,500 kilometers. The maneuver helped lay the foundation for the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution. Cai said the spirit forged through the sacrifices of Chinese Communists and Red Army soldiers continues to inspire the Chinese people to overcome difficulties and advance from victory to victory. The exhibition provides an important platform for education on ideals and convictions, patriotism and revolutionary traditions, he said, calling for carrying forward the Long March spirit on the new journey. The exhibition comprises seven main sections, including the Zunyi Meeting, major military operations and the enduring legacy of the Long March. English captions accompany each exhibit. The exhibition takes up approximately 3,300 square meters on the western side of the museum's third floor, with a display route stretching more than 760 meters. It features 875 cultural relics or sets of relics, a substantial increase from previous exhibitions in 2006 and 2016. The museum also said it is displaying 186 historical documents, 357 photographs and charts, 73 artworks and 16 videos. According to the museum, more than 300 relics and documents are being exhibited for the first time, accounting for approximately 28 percent of the total number of relics and documents on display. The exhibition also presents 60 stories from the Long March. It features 14 scenes depicting key episodes, including the Battle of the Xiangjiang River, the Zunyi Meeting and the Four Crossings of the Chishui River. About 600 people, including officials, military personnel and representatives from various walks of life, attended the opening ceremony. Cai and other leaders toured the exhibition with members of the public afterward.

item.title: Xi sends congratulatory letter to 48th WorldSkills Competition
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
BEIJING, Sept. 22 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping sent a congratulatory letter on Tuesday to the 48th WorldSkills Competition. Xi noted that a new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial transformation is advancing rapidly, exerting a profound impact on global skills development. Closely aligned with the needs of industries, the WorldSkills Competition provides a useful platform for skilled professionals from various countries to hone their skills and learn from each other, Xi said. Xi stressed that China will take the opportunity of hosting this year's competition to encourage and guide more workers, especially young people, to pursue a path to success through skills. "China is willing to strengthen exchanges and cooperation with all parties, promote the development of the WorldSkills movement, and better contribute to global economic growth and the improvement of people's well-being," Xi said. The 48th WorldSkills Competition opened in Shanghai the same day under the theme "Master Skills Change Your Future." Hosted by WorldSkills International and jointly organized by China's Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and the Shanghai Municipal People's Government, the competition will also feature the WorldSkills Conference and WorldSkills Expo.

item.title: Xi extends greetings ahead of farmers' harvest festival
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
BEIJING, Sept. 22 (Xinhua) -- Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, has extended festive greetings and sincere regards on behalf of the CPC Central Committee to farmers and people working on agricultural and rural fronts ahead of the ninth Chinese farmers' harvest festival. Xi, also Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, stressed the importance of solid efforts to advance all-around rural revitalization and ensure that farmers live happier and better lives. Xi noted that this year, China's summer grain output hit a new record and early rice output remained stable, while a bumper autumn harvest is within sight. Party committees and governments at all levels should work to ensure that policies aimed at strengthening agriculture, benefiting farmers and enriching rural areas deliver greater outcomes and enhance the overall production capacity, quality and performance of agriculture, he said. Efforts should be made to expand channels for rural residents to increase incomes and build a beautiful and harmonious countryside for people to live and work in, based on local conditions, Xi said. The Chinese farmers' harvest festival is the first national festival created specifically for the country's farmers. This year's festival falls on Wednesday. Launched in 2018, the festival coincides with the Autumnal Equinox each year, which is one of the 24 solar terms of the Chinese lunisolar calendar and usually falls between Sept. 22 and 24 during the country's agricultural harvest season.

item.title: Xi's upcoming U.S. visit to chart course for bilateral ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
* Since Trump's return to the White House in 2025, the Chinese and U.S. heads of state have stayed in close contact, speaking by phone many times, exchanging letters on several occasions and meeting face to face twice since late last year. * Despite frictions and challenges, China-U.S. trade has demonstrated strong resilience. In the second quarter of this year, bilateral trade in goods grew 13.7 percent year on year. As of July this year, U.S. companies had established more than 84,000 enterprises in China. * In just over two and a half years, more than 50,000 young Americans from all 50 states have been invited to travel to different parts of China. They have toured smart factories, visited rural communities and experienced everyday life in places far from home. For many, the journeys have led to new friendships with Chinese peers. BEIJING, Sept. 22 (Xinhua) -- At the invitation of U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping will pay a state visit to the United States from Sept. 23 to 25, marking an exchange of visits between the two leaders within six months. As changes unseen in a century are accelerating and uncertainties continue to grow around the world, the visit is expected to bring greater stability and predictability to China-U.S. relations and beyond. CONSTRUCTIVE STRATEGIC STABILITY China-U.S. ties have been widely regarded as the world's most important bilateral relationship. More than 50 years ago, leaders from both countries, with remarkable courage and political vision, took the historic step of breaking the ice. Since then, the relationship has repeatedly found a way forward despite tensions and setbacks, with head-of-state diplomacy consistently providing strategic guidance. Foreign students attending Sharing Session: Tales of People-to-People Bonds Between China and the U.S. & Re-China Dialogue visit an exhibition highlighting friendly exchanges between the civilian sectors of China and the United States at the Overseas Chinese History Museum of China in Beijing, capital of China, June 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Jin Liangkuai) In recent years, China-U.S. relations have weathered ups and downs. How the world's two major countries manage their relationship matters far beyond their own borders. Hosting Trump in Beijing in May, Xi underscored the responsibilities shouldered by both countries in these changing times. "Can China and the United States overcome the Thucydides Trap and create a new paradigm of major-country relations? Can we meet global challenges together and provide greater stability for the world? Can we build a bright future together for our bilateral relations in the interest of the well-being of the two peoples and the future of humanity? These are the questions vital to history, to the world and to the people," said Xi. Xi has repeatedly said that the broad Pacific Ocean is vast enough to embrace both China and the United States. He has also urged the two sides to be partners and friends, and work together to accomplish more great and concrete things for the good of the two countries and the whole world. Since Trump's return to the White House in 2025, the two leaders have stayed in close contact, speaking by phone many times, exchanging letters on several occasions and meeting face to face twice since late last year. "I look forward to working together with you to set the course and steer the giant ship of China-U.S. relations, so as to make 2026 a historic, landmark year that opens up a new chapter in China-U.S. relations," Xi said in his meeting with Trump in May. It was during their Beijing meeting that the two leaders agreed on a new vision of building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, providing strategic guidance for bilateral ties over the next three years and beyond. "The building of a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability should not be a mere slogan, but concrete action taken by both sides toward the same goal," Xi said. He outlined the "constructive strategic stability" as a positive stability with cooperation as the mainstay, a sound stability with moderate competition, a constant stability with manageable differences, and an enduring stability with promises of peace. "The most important thing that comes out of leader-level meetings is that when the two leaders meet, they're able to build trust, and when they build trust, then everything else becomes easier," said Sean Stein, president of the U.S.-China Business Council. "So for us, that's the most important thing we're looking for when President Xi travels to Washington to meet President Trump," he added. WIN-WIN COOPERATION As China and the United States share broad common interests and vast potential for cooperation, Xi has emphasized the need to expand mutually beneficial cooperation, strengthen dialogue and consultation, and turn shared interests into concrete outcomes. China-U.S. economic ties are mutually beneficial and win-win in nature, Xi said in his meeting with Trump in May. During his state visit to China, Trump was accompanied by top U.S. executives, including Apple's Tim Cook, Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Tesla's Elon Musk, whom he called outstanding representatives from the U.S. business community. A visitor looks at a product at a Chinese company's booth during MAGIC, a major U.S. trade show for apparel, footwear and accessories, in Las Vegas, the United States, Aug. 10, 2026. (Photo by Zeng Hui/Xinhua) "China will only open its door wider," Xi said during the meeting with Trump. American companies are deeply involved in China's reform and opening up, and the U.S. side is welcome to enhance mutually beneficial cooperation, he added. "As the world's two largest, most dynamic and most technologically advanced economies, it's just impossible for the U.S. and Chinese economies to function as well without a strong and viable relationship with the other, so it's absolutely essential," said Stein. Despite frictions and challenges, China-U.S. trade has demonstrated strong resilience. In the second quarter of this year, bilateral trade in goods grew 13.7 percent year on year. As of July this year, U.S. companies had established more than 84,000 enterprises in China. "What has happened demonstrates yet again that the description of China-U.S. cooperation benefiting both sides and confrontation hurting both sides reflects a common sense that has been repeatedly proven by experience, and the vision of China and the United States helping each other succeed and prosper together is a tangible prospect within reach," Xi said in a phone conversation with Trump in 2025. This year marks the launch of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) for economic and social development, and the 250th founding anniversary of the United States. As both countries enter pivotal stages of their respective development, new opportunities for cooperation are emerging. In July, a delegation of Chinese business leaders traveled to Salt Lake City, Chicago and Washington, D.C., where they met with representatives of more than 120 U.S. companies and organizations. Their discussions underscored that the appetite for cooperation remains strong. Across the U.S. business community, there is growing recognition of the vast potential for Chinese and U.S. companies to work together in cutting-edge fields, from green energy and the digital economy to artificial intelligence and biomedicine. Kate Sullivan, executive director of the Greater Columbus Chinese Chamber of Commerce, pointed to Illuminate USA, a joint-venture solar panel manufacturer in Columbus, Ohio, as a success story of China-U.S. cooperation. "It is the epitome of advanced manufacturing in the state of Ohio, drawing on multiple strengths of Chinese manufacturing and supply chains," she said. "It makes sense for the United States and China to be in business together. It's not an emotional decision there. It's business. Supply and demand." Looking ahead, business representatives also voiced expectations for a more stable environment for bilateral cooperation. "We hope the two heads of state will maintain strategic communication, bringing greater stability, stronger confidence and a longer-term outlook to markets and businesses in both countries," said Wang Qi, chairman of the U.S.-China Green Energy Council. PEOPLE-TO-PEOPLE EXCHANGES Xi has consistently emphasized that the foundation and future of China-U.S. relations ultimately lie in the connections between the two peoples. "Though geographically far apart, our peoples boast a long history of friendly exchanges," Xi said in a speech at a welcoming dinner hosted by local governments and friendly organizations in Seattle in 2015. Over the years, Xi has maintained close personal ties with people from all walks of life in the United States. In 2015, Xi visited Lincoln High School in the U.S. port city of Tacoma. Without a tie, he presented gifts to the students, including books on China, a ping-pong table, and his personal invitation for the students to visit China. American students visit a park during a music and cultural exchange camp between young people of China and the United States in Changzhou City, east China's Jiangsu Province, July 14, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Bo) In 2023, before the Welcome Dinner by Friendly Organizations in San Francisco, Xi met with veterans of the Flying Tigers and descendants of late General Joseph Stilwell, whose stories have become an important part of the history of China-U.S. friendship. In 2024, in his reply to a letter from Lamont Repollet, president of Kean University in the United States, Xi encouraged universities in China and the United States to strengthen exchanges and cooperation and contribute to China-U.S. friendship. During this year's Spring Festival, Xi replied to friends in the U.S. state of Iowa and sent them a Chinese New Year card with festive greetings, continuing their warm exchange of New Year wishes for the third consecutive year. In 2023, during his visit to San Francisco, Xi announced that China was ready to invite 50,000 young Americans to China on exchange and study programs in the next five years. "We hope that our two peoples will make more visits, contacts and exchanges and write new stories of friendship in the new era," he said. The invitation was warmly received by young people in the United States. In just over two and a half years, more than 50,000 young Americans from all 50 states have traveled to China. Their trips have taken them to different parts of the country. They have toured smart factories, visited rural communities and experienced everyday life in places far from home. For many, the journeys have also led to new friendships with Chinese peers. "I am particularly grateful to President Xi for his initiative of 50,000 in five years. I think that is possibly one of the most consequential initiatives in the last 20 years," said Luca Berrone, a four-decade-long friend of Xi in Iowa. "I believe that people-to-people exchanges, particularly between China and the United States, are fundamental in continuing to strengthen the relationship, to improve understanding and acceptance," he said. (Video reporters: Mu Xuyao, Meng Jing, Xu Yang, Liu Chunhui, Yang Zhigang, Zhao Xu, Hu Yousong and You Zhixin; Video editors: Mu Xuyao, Liu Xiaorui, Zhao Tianlin, Wang Houyuan, Shi Peng and Shang Yang)

item.title: China urges Japan to stop any attempt at "remilitarization": spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-21
BEIJING, Sept. 21 (Xinhua) -- China urges Japan to deeply reflect on its history of aggression, heed the calls of regional countries and stop pursuing any attempt at "remilitarization," Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Monday. Guo made the remarks at a regular media briefing when asked about reports that the Russian Foreign Ministry had notified Japan over the U.S. deployment of the Typhon mid-range missile system in Kyushu, stressing that the deployment is unacceptable, urging Japan to fully recognize the outcomes of World War II and stop "remilitarization." "The Typhon mid-range missile system is a strategic offensive weapon, and Japan's introduction of the system is yet another piece of evidence of its accelerated 'remilitarization,'" Guo said. Guo said the move increases risks of military confrontation and an arms race, threatens strategic balance and regional stability, and undermines the legitimate security interests of neighboring countries. The international community is highly vigilant after the move, and people in multiple Asian countries have voiced opposition to it, Guo said. China has repeatedly lodged strong protests with Japan through diplomatic channels and recently sent a diplomatic note to the Japanese side to reiterate its solemn position, he added.

item.title: China urges Japan to deeply reflect on history of aggression: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-18
BEIJING, Sept. 18 (Xinhua) -- China urges Japan to face up to and deeply reflect on its history of aggression, and gain the trust of its Asian neighbors and the international community with concrete actions, foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told a press briefing on Friday. The September 18th Incident 95 years ago marked the start of Japan's 14-year invasion of China. Ninety-five years ago today, Guo said, Japanese militarists launched aggression against China, and they were met by the courageous resistance of the Chinese people, which lifted the curtain of the eastern theater of the World Anti-Fascist War. Noting the September 18th Incident was a war plot long concealed by the Japanese government from the Japanese public, Guo said the vast majority of the Japanese people did not learn the truth until the Tokyo Trials, which opened 80 years ago. The increasingly prevalent historical denialism in Japan is truly troubling, and the danger is self-evident, Guo noted. Denialism not just reflects serious regression in Japan's perception of history, but also indicates alarmingly an organized attempt to turn back the wheel of history with clear political motives, said Guo, adding that the real purpose is to keep the Japanese public from the truth, and clear the path for Japan to escape the straitjacket of the postwar system and rearm itself. Denying the crime of aggression is to challenge historical conclusions and undermine the post-war international order, Guo said, stressing that all countries in the region, including China, must remain highly vigilant, not allow Japanese militarism to resurface, and not let historical tragedies repeat themselves. "We must work together to uphold the outcomes of the World War II victory and jointly safeguard peace", Guo added.
